scope: Initial capability-family inventory; not exhaustive and not proof of parity.

sources.reviewScope: README, repository tree, license boundaries, budget reservation, Redis Cluster cache and PostgreSQL schema sources; runtime equivalence not reviewed
sources.licenseBoundary: MIT outside enterprise/; enterprise/ has a separate license. Preserve notices for any copied MIT implementation.

sources.reviewScope: Provider/native versus canonical identity, type filtering, reasoning_options, public HTTP validators and OpenRouter decision omission; schema source ref is separate from live asset provenance.
sources.licenseBoundary: MIT; snapshot notice and upstream attribution retained.

sources.reviewScope: Routes, Services, Plugin Configs, precedence and deployment modes; traffic-resource concepts adapted locally, no Lua plugin implementation copied.
sources.licenseBoundary: Apache-2.0 upstream; source references retained. This adaptation does not copy APISIX code.

capabilities.remaining: Original README artwork, RedRouter CLI identity, port 25050, loopback bind, ~/.red/router storage and service install/status/uninstall are restored locally. CI and a published mise/red-dev replacement remain pending. The original dashboard experience still needs contract-by-contract restoration.
acceptance: RedRouter dashboard navigation and complete setup/provider/combo/key/usage workflows remain available.
Documented RedRouter CLI and service commands work from the published package.

capabilities.remaining: Remote-router discovery persists chat and native decision catalogs per credential, preserves nested IDs under the public red prefix, and forwards native decision requests one hop at a time. Remote capabilities stay authoritative; opaque chat and decision routing follows instance/tenant provider priority. Product regression and HTTP-fixture validation are in CI, not an external credentialed federation parity claim. Legacy embedded cache/proxy migration remains unresolved. Audit every other provider identity, auth/refresh, entitlements, modalities and wire format.
acceptance: No provider identity is substituted with a different account product.
Model discoveries persist and are scoped to the connection/key.
Fixture contracts pass in CI; credentialed smoke is recorded separately.
Gemini CLI stays retired as a provider; Antigravity remains supported.

capabilities.remaining: Three discovery routes restored locally; CI pending. Key identity/MCP discovery uses persisted-key auth. Catalog/capabilities project the existing authorized model list and explicitly do not claim complete baseline compatibility. Remaining: account metadata/grouping, recommendations, collapsed variants, per-key ID-format application, shared legacy catalog version headers, stable instance identity and global reasoning/session discovery. Tests cover handler projections and authorization delegation, not the full database-backed catalog or credentialed provider behavior.
acceptance: Restore client feature discovery, grouped/account-scoped catalogs and key-role/MCP discovery contracts.
Compare authenticated and unauthorized responses with RedRouter baseline fixtures.
Never expose a different key's identity, permissions or connected accounts.

capabilities.remaining: Compare request/response/stream/error semantics, tools, reasoning, images, audio, video, files, batches and realtime by provider; HTTP route presence is insufficient.
acceptance: Protocol fixtures cover success, streaming cancellation, tool calls and upstream errors.
Unsupported capabilities are explicit; translation endpoints remain supported.

capabilities.remaining: Preserve RedRouter model/account failover while comparing strategies, retry boundaries, context routing, quotas and connection affinity.
acceptance: Do not retry a request after emitting upstream bytes or replay ambiguous billable writes.
Account/model errors do not disable a whole provider.
Equivalent requests produce equivalent routing and error contracts under fixtures.

capabilities.remaining: Ported implementations exist. Preserve optional evaluator behavior, typed decision contracts and routing controls; real-provider validation remains separate.
acceptance: System One remains distinct from ordinary chat.
Unavailable evaluation never becomes an implicit approval.
Optional decision routing preserves normal behavior when disabled.

capabilities.remaining: RED_ROUTER_BRANDING precedence and --reddb-* token acceptance are restored locally with tests/unit/branding-product-contract.test.ts. CI is pending. The original dashboard design and visual token consumers still need restoration and UI validation.
acceptance: Existing RedRouter branding path and token vocabulary are honored.
Logo, login, favicon and theme work through the RedRouter settings flow.

capabilities.remaining: OIDC source is present; no SAML dashboard implementation was located in the integrated tree. Compare resource isolation, keys, teams/organizations, roles and audit behavior independently.
acceptance: RedRouter password/OIDC/SAML workflows and resource scoping are preserved.
Cross-user and cross-organization reads/writes are denied.
Enterprise capabilities requiring independent implementation are tracked separately from licensed upstream code.

capabilities.remaining: Compare model/account restrictions, key lifecycle, rate/token/spend budgets, reservations and reconciliation, including concurrent requests.
acceptance: Concurrent requests cannot independently spend the same remaining budget.
Retries, cancellations and stream termination reconcile reservations exactly once.
Budget scope and reset windows match the documented API.

capabilities.remaining: RedRouter-owned SQLite outbox, stable IDs, signed HTTPS webhook, instant/window aggregation and management API are implemented for request_cost_ledger rows. Window high-water marks and delivery lease fencing need CI verification. This is costed-requests-only, not complete usage or billing parity: some request paths still do not write priced ledger rows. SQS, Kafka and RedDB queue transports (one interface, delivery id as message identity, credentials encrypted with the log-export secret primitives), test/deliveries/retry endpoints and the dashboard page are implemented and covered by native tests with injected clients; they have not been exercised against a real SQS, Kafka broker or RedDB, and the dashboard has not been rendered in a browser. Key-tag filters (Friday filtered on API key tags) and a Friday-database import of existing sinks remain. Log export is a separate capability.
acceptance: Preserve signed webhook, SQS, Kafka and RedDB delivery contracts.
Retries keep stable delivery IDs and do not duplicate billable usage.
Trace and cost attribution survive model/account fallback.

capabilities.remaining: SQLite is the initial backend. Optional Redis coordination does not establish distributed persistence. Audit baseline SQL abstraction, then implement durable shared state, migration ownership and replica-safe coordination.
acceptance: Single-node SQLite remains fully usable.
Two replicas enforce one shared budget and lease ownership under races.
Usage/job idempotency survives crashes and retries.
Rolling schema changes and replica failover preserve request correctness.

capabilities.remaining: Compare cache isolation, invalidation, streaming behavior, semantic cache, backpressure, concurrency and memory. Measure the RedRouter implementation; do not copy upstream benchmark claims.
acceptance: Cached results never cross key/tenant/policy boundaries.
Latency and throughput measurements include workload, hardware and error rate.
Cache failure has an explicit bounded fallback.

capabilities.remaining: Compare RedRouter MCP tool contracts with imported server tools, upstream MCP gateway/client behavior, A2A versions, skills, memory and agent workflows.
acceptance: Legacy RedRouter tools preserve schemas, permissions and results.
MCP server and outbound MCP gateway capabilities are tracked separately.
A2A clients validate lifecycle, authentication and streaming behavior.

capabilities.remaining: Compare guardrails, hooks, prompt management, evaluations and observability integrations; identify OSS versus separately licensed implementations.
acceptance: Opt-in features do not silently alter disabled request paths.
Hooks and guardrails preserve stream cleanup and sanitized error contracts.
Behavioral comparisons include denied, degraded and timeout paths.

capabilities.remaining: RedRouter npm upload is restored, but a post-publication install/registry check is missing. Inventory container, desktop, service installation and SDK/client compatibility separately.
acceptance: Publish RedRouter through its GitHub workflow using the same verified tarball.
Verify public registry metadata, downloaded checksum and clean installation.
Run RedRouter workflow regressions alongside inherited feature tests in CI.
No claim of release stability from upstream tests or upload acceptance alone.

capabilities.remaining: Local adaptations require the exact-commit CI gates. Public discovery does not prove credential entitlement or a successful typed decision evaluation; unimplemented decision protocols remain non-executable. Canonical links are optional, and models.dev does not define a complete HTTP parameter schema. Multi-process/replica invalidation remains outside these process-local catalog guarantees.
acceptance: Bundled metadata works offline and never creates connections or enables models.
Provider-native IDs and declared endpoint/credential/payload contracts survive enrichment and router federation.
Prices and controls stay scoped to the actual provider product and user overrides win.
Decision discovery stays distinct from chat and exposes only implemented protocols authorized to the calling key.
ETag/304 and failed refresh retain one atomic last-good metadata snapshot; authorization changes invalidate authenticated fallback.

capabilities.remaining: Reusable visibility/priority profiles now attach explicitly at instance and owner-tenant levels, with local overrides and effective origins. Profiles do not configure cache, budgets, key restrictions, endpoints or payload transforms. Declarative promotion and split control/data-plane deployment remain unimplemented. Preview does not prove live dispatch or APISIX parity. Exact-commit CI is required.
acceptance: The existing runtime resolvers determine mode, priority and key/tenant scope; owner pins remain authoritative.
Provider/native model IDs and one-hop System One federation remain unchanged.
Preview never sends a completion or decision and returns no credentials, token hashes, headers or provider-specific secrets.
Disabled and cooling connections remain visible as configuration metadata without being treated as eligible credentials.
Scope changes and failed refreshes remove stale routes and connection metadata; model examples come from the authorized catalog.
Profile creation does not attach or enable anything; edits update all attachments and invalidate discovery while explicit local overrides remain.
Attached profiles cannot be deleted, and tenant admins cannot replace owner profile pins.
